data.title: Tesla produces 7,000 Model Ys in one week at Giga Berlin
data.description:
Tesla has built 7,000 Model Ys during a single week at Giga Berlin, reaching a new production milestone at the German factory that now supplies Canadian customers.

The announcement came from Tesla Manufacturing on X, which credited employees as the plant continues increasing output.

At that weekly pace, Giga Berlin would produce approximately 364,000 Model Ys annually, coming close to the >375,000 annualized figure in the Q3 2026 shareholder deck.

Giga Berlin previously reached 5,000 Model Ys in a week in March 2023, followed by 6,000 in early 2024.

The latest production figure should come as no surprise and follows months of preparations in Germany. Tesla announced in June that it planned another 20% output increase beginning in October, targeting approximately 7,500 vehicles weekly and adding 1,000 employees to support the expansion.

By September, workers had been assigned three extra shifts as the company worked toward that goal. At the time, the factory was producing fewer than 6,500 vehicles weekly, according to our earlier coverage. The newly announced total brings Berlin closer to its stated target.

For Canada, the milestone comes at an important factory. Tesla began bringing German-built Model Ys into the country in September 2025, with the first shipment arriving through Halifax. The switch allowed Tesla to avoid Canada’s 25% counter-tariff on vehicles manufactured in the United States.

That sourcing change helped Tesla bring Canadian prices down, but also made deliveries dependent on shipments crossing the Atlantic. In July, we reported that estimated arrival dates for Canadian orders had moved into December, with some configurations showing January 2027. Those were the estimates at the time, rather than a new update from Tesla.

Berlin also supplies more than 30 markets, so its production serves customers well beyond Canada.

Related Articles:

  • First shipment of German-made Tesla Model Y arrives in Canada
  • Tesla adds shifts at Giga Berlin to boost Model Y production
  • Tesla announces second Giga Berlin production and hiring expansion in months

data.title: Tesla Hosting Electric Summon Halloween Events Across North America This Weekend
data.description:
Tesla has announced a series of Halloween-themed events at its stores across Canada and the United States this weekend, giving families a chance to experience the automaker’s new Halloween Mode software update through interactive activities.

According to Tesla’s official event listings, the “Electric Summon” events will take place on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at locations across North America.

The events will feature family-friendly activities, seasonal refreshments, costume competitions and an opportunity for children to collect candy from decorated Tesla vehicles.

Tesla is also encouraging owners to participate by decorating their vehicles’ front trunks, or frunks, and handing out candy to children. Parking will be available on a first come, first served basis.

Visitors will also have an opportunity to explore Tesla’s new Halloween Mode through an interactive activity card, highlighting features introduced in software update 2026.38.3.

Halloween Mode includes a ghost costume for the on-screen vehicle, themed wraps, a Halloween light show and a new lock sound. Its Trick or Treat feature also activates spooky sounds and flickering lights when visitors approach.

Other additions include Photobooth effects and the ability to broadcast a creepy voice remotely through the Tesla app. A Tesla FSD software engineer has also confirmed the update will reach vehicles running the Full Self-Driving (FSD) software branch.

Tesla says attendees must submit an RSVP to reserve their spot, with space limited at participating locations.

You can check if Tesla is hosting an event near you at Tesla.com/events.

Related Articles:

  • Tesla Rolls Out Halloween Mode With Spooky Sounds, Lights and More [2026.38.3]
  • Tesla Says FSD Owners Won’t Miss Out on Halloween Mode
  • Tesla Teases Spooky Halloween Software Update

data.title: Tesla offering FSD demo drives at Superchargers in Canada
data.description:
Tesla appears to be expanding beyond offering demo drives of its vehicles at Superchargers, with the company now highlighting Full Self-Driving (FSD) at stations in Canada.

The unannounced event was sSotted by Tesla owner and enthusiast Nic Cruz Patane on X, who shared of a photo of a sign at his local Supercharger in Mississauga (North Service Road) inviting visitors to “Experience Full Self-Driving (Supervised).”

The event is different than previous ones held by Tesla, where prospective buyers can test drive Tesla vehicles, rather than focusing specifically on the company’s advanced driver assistance technology.

Tesla appears to be building on that approach by using Supercharger stations not only to introduce customers to its vehicles, but also to demonstrate what FSD can do.

Tesla already includes FSD (Supervised) on all vehicles available through its self-serve demo drive program. However, the Ontario sighting marks a shift in how the company is promoting the experience, with FSD itself becoming the main attraction.

The shift comes after Tesla revealed that FSD’s attach rate on new vehicle purchases had climbed above 75%. The figure indicates that more than three-quarters of new Tesla buyers are opting to add the driver assistance package to their purchase.

With FSD adoption already reaching those levels among new buyers, dedicated events at Superchargers could also help Tesla reach existing owners who have yet to subscribe to the software. Unlike traditional vehicle demo drives, these events put the focus on experiencing FSD rather than buying a new car.

Related Articles

  • Tesla Hosting One-Day Demo Drive Event at Canmore Supercharger This Saturday
  • Tesla FSD Attach Rate Tops 75% as Musk Hopes for EU-Wide Approval by Q1

data.title: AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon Push Back on FCC Satellite-to-Phone Rule Changes
data.description:
AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon have joined wireless industry group CTIA in challenging parts of a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) proposal to expand satellite-to-phone services, as SpaceX pursues access to 80,000 US cell towers for Starlink Mobile. 

The companies raised concerns about interference, carrier control and the use of existing 5G frequencies.

According to an official CTIA filing dated October 22, representatives met separately with advisers to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr and Commissioners Anna Gomez and Olivia Trusty on October 20. The group urged regulators to revise several provisions before moving forward.

The discussions follow the FCC’s October 8 draft proposal to expand Supplemental Coverage from Space (SCS), which allows satellites to connect directly with ordinary phones using mobile carriers’ licensed frequencies. The proposal would open another 482 megahertz of spectrum, increasing the number of eligible bands from five to 13.

CTIA specifically requested the removal of Time-Division Duplex (TDD) frequencies, including the 2.5 GHz and 3.45 GHz bands. The group argued these frequencies are technically unsuitable for satellite service and currently support wireless connectivity for more than 300 million users.

At the same time, CTIA opposed replacing existing spectrum leasing requirements with agreements allowing satellite and terrestrial operators to share frequencies. It asked the FCC to preserve carrier consent, control and termination rights, while maintaining access to regulatory enforcement.

Despite those objections, CTIA acknowledged that satellite connectivity could extend coverage into remote communities and areas affected by disasters. SpaceX has not publicly responded to the filing.

The draft is scheduled for consideration at the FCC’s October 29 open meeting. 

The letters comes just days after the FCC approved SpaceX’s acquisition of Tristar’s AWS-3 spectrum, a move that would allow Starlink Mobile to challenge the major carriers in the U.S.

Related Articles:

  • SpaceX in Talks to Access 80,000 US Cell Towers for Starlink Mobile: Report
  • FCC Approves SpaceX Deal for Tristar’s AWS-3 Spectrum to Expand Starlink Direct-to-Device Service

data.title: Tesla Megapacks Arrive at Massive 400MWh Battery Storage Project in Belgium
data.description:
A utility-scale battery storage site in Belgium has started taking delivery of Tesla Megapack 2 units. The 400 MWh project will help balance the grid and accelerate the rollout of renewable energy.

Massive Tesla Megapack 2s are finally arriving at the Langerlo battery pack in Genk, Eastern Belgium. Reports indicate that most of the 106 XL batteries are now ready for deployment.

The energy storage project can deliver up to 100 MW of electricity to the grid. With a total capacity of 400 MWh, the site can operate at full capacity for four hours before the batteries are depleted.

Construction is expected to be completed in 2027. The Megapacks will store electricity when supply exceeds demand and release it when demand rises. Thus, the grid remains stable.

The Langerlo project is a win for the environment. The energy storage site was a former coal-fired power plant. It will connect to the grid via existing connections. The old power plant, the last of its kind in Belgium, burned its last coal in March 2016.

Storm is the developer behind the project. It is investing about 330 million euros in Langerlo and another site in Ruien.

Tesla’s battery business is booming, according to an update CEO Elon Musk shared at the last company earnings call. Deployment reached 13.7 GWh in Q3 2026, with revenue of $2.88 billion.

Tesla began producing the Megapack 3 in Texas in August. The American company expects demand to surge as data centers worldwide deploy batteries to maintain high uptime.

data.title: NHTSA Proposes Easing Manual Lighting Control Rules for Driverless Vehicles Like Cybercab
data.description:
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has proposed changes to federal vehicle lighting regulations that could affect Tesla’s Cybercab, which is already facing a separate audit over its road-legal certification. 

The proposal would remove certain manual lighting control requirements for autonomous vehicles designed without steering wheels or pedals.

Under the current Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 108, vehicles must meet requirements for manually operated lighting controls. These include switches for turn signals, hazard warning lights, and headlight beam selection, even though fully driverless vehicles may have no human driver to operate them.

NHTSA’s proposed changes would limit those requirements to vehicles equipped with manual driving controls. Vehicles operating exclusively through an automated driving system (ADS) would therefore have greater flexibility in how their lighting systems are designed, without needing conventional switches intended for human drivers.

The agency explained that the proposed revisions are intended “to remove unnecessary requirements and to provide design flexibility without impact on vehicle safety.”

The changes could be significant for Tesla’s Cybercab, which was designed without a steering wheel or pedals. NHTSA opened an audit in September examining how Tesla self-certified the vehicle under existing federal safety standards, with the automaker subsequently receiving additional time to respond. 

Beyond removing certain manual control requirements, NHTSA is also proposing optional cyan-coloured exterior lights to identify vehicles operating without human supervision. The blue-green colour was selected partly because it is distinct from the blue lights used by law enforcement.

Manufacturers would not be required to install them, and Mercedes-Benz previously tested similar lights on public roads in California between 2023 and 2025.

The proposal also includes changes to headlight testing voltages and removes requirements governing vertical headlight arrangements. Tesla has not commented on the proposal.

The proposed regulations are scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on October 26, 2026, followed by a 30-day public comment period through regulations.gov. 

Related Articles:

data.title: New Tesla Roadster Goes on Public Display for the First Time at Petersen Museum
data.description:
The new Tesla Roadster, whose cold gas thrusters Lars Moravy says are built for production, will go on public display for the first time this weekend at the Petersen Automotive Museum in Los Angeles.

The museum says the Roadster will sit in its main lobby from Saturday, October 24 through Tuesday, October 27, a limited four-day appearance.

According to the Petersen’s vehicle page, it is the same car that shared the stage with Elon Musk and the Tesla team at the unveiling in McGregor, Texas.

The museum describes it as the first chance for the public to see the vehicle up close. The Petersen is at 6060 Wilshire Blvd and is open daily from 10 AM to 6 PM.

Since the Roadster will be sitting in the lobby, a ticket is not needed to view the car this weekend.

For more on the car itself, here is what we’ve learned about the new Roadster since its reveal, and Musk’s claim that the Roadster will perform its stunts autonomously.

The Petersen previously added a Cybertruck to its “Inside Tesla” exhibit in 2023.

data.title: Tesla Robotaxi expands Austin service to COTA, extends hours to 1 AM ahead of F1 weekend
data.description:
Tesla has stretched its Robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, to cover Circuit of the Americas (COTA) and run until 1 AM, less than a week after Cybercab rides were extended to midnight in the city.

The change was first shared on X by Sawyer Merritt, just as Austin gets ready to host the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix at the track this weekend.

According to an updated to the Robotaxi mobile app, the updated service area map now includes the area around the racetrack.

Alongside the service area expansion, customers can now request a Robotaxi until 1 AM, an hour later than the previous midnight cut-off, which had only been in place since October 17.

Before that, Robotaxi rides in Austin ended at 11 PM, which is also when Cybercab service wrapped up each night when the two-seat vehicles first joined the fleet.

COTA sits southeast of downtown Austin, and several other X users also posted that the geofence now reaches the track ahead of race weekend.

The Austin update follows a busy week for the program, with Tesla publishing a Robotaxi safety report claiming zero injuries and confirming on its earnings call that the Cybercab is heading to Dallas next month.

Tesla’s Model Y Robotaxis already operate in Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa, while the Cybercab is currently only available in Austin.

Related Articles:

  • Tesla Cybercab Extends Daily Operating Hours to Midnight in Austin
  • Tesla Cybercab heading to Dallas next month
  • Tesla Launches Robotaxi Safety Report, Claims Zero Injuries Over 3.1 Million Autonomous Miles

data.title: Tesla launches Supercharger for Business and Semi Charging for Business in Canada
data.description:
Tesla has brought Supercharger for Business to Canada, along with its Semi Charging for Business program, so Canadian companies can now buy Tesla chargers for their own sites.

Livio Caputo of Tesla’s Charging for Business team shared the Canadian launch on LinkedIn, as first reported by EVwire.

“The goal is to offer Charging for Business in every market where Tesla runs charging, 55+ countries and growing, with the same hardware, software and service we use ourselves,” Caputo wrote.

For passenger vehicles, Canadian hosts have to buy at least four Supercharger posts, according to Tesla’s Canadian Supercharger for Business page.

Tesla’s Canadian Supercharger for Business page also says the white-labelled stalls work with all EVs, can show up on the in-car map and come with a 97% uptime guarantee, while V4 posts are rated at up to 500 kW.

On the truck side, businesses need a minimum of two posts and can pick between the Megacharger and the Basecharger.

Tesla’s Semi Charging for Business page rates the Megacharger at up to 1.2 MW, which Tesla says can restore as much as 60% of a Semi’s range within half an hour.

The slower Basecharger, rated at 120 kW, targets depot and overnight charging and takes about four hours to restore that same 60%, with deliveries estimated to start in early 2027.

Owners can use their own installer with help from a Tesla Design Engineer, or have Tesla do the install, and then set pricing through Tesla’s portal while Tesla handles servicing.

Neither Canadian page lists pricing, and buyers are directed to a contact form instead.

In B.C., R.R. Plett Trucking is planning Canada’s first Tesla Megachargers in Langley and Kamloops.

The carrier expects to take delivery of 12 Tesla Semis in June 2027.

Related Articles:

  • Canada’s first Tesla Semi Megachargers to begin construction next month in B.C.
